olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Gabriel and Arnaldo color segments on a triangular net: endpoints at triangle vertices, segment made of one or more sides, no overlap with previous. Gabriel goes first; player unable to move loses. Find a winning strategy.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2017

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Call $(a,b)$ with $a<391$ a \textit{pupusa} pair if $\text{lcm}(a,b)>\text{lcm}(a,391)$. Find the minimum $b$ over all pupusa pairs.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2017

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $\triangle ABC$ with $D$ = foot of altitude from $A$; $\ell$ = line through midpoints of $BC$ and $AC$; $E$ = reflection of $D$ over $\ell$. Prove the circumcenter of $\triangle ABC$ lies on line $AE$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2017

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Right $\triangle ABC$ with $\angle ABC=90^\circ$ and $AB<BC$; $B'$ = reflection of $B$ over $AC$; $M$ = midpoint of $AC$; $D\in BM$ with $BD=AC$. Prove $B'C$ bisects $\angle MB'D$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2017

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Susana and Brenda alternate building a polynomial. Susana picks $n_0$, writes $P_0(x)=n_0$. Each turn: pick a new positive integer and either add or subtract it times the appropriate power of $x$. First to write a polynomial with an integer root wins. Find a winning strategy.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2017

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Tita the Frog sits on integer $k>1$. From $n$, she hops to $f(n)+g(n)$ where $f(n)$ and $g(n)$ are the largest and smallest prime factors of $n$. Find all $k$ for which Tita visits infinitely many distinct integers.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2017
